title: Compiler-Directed Whole-System Persistence
problem: Nonvolatile memory systems face crash consistency issues when stores are evicted out-of-order; power failure between out-of-order persistence of younger and older stores prevents correct program resumption.
motivation: NVM technologies offer density and durability benefits but require performant and programmer-friendly crash consistency solutions.
method: cWSP partitions the entire software stack (applications, OS, runtime) into recoverable epochs using compiler/architecture codesign. The compiler optimizes register checkpointing while simple hardware support expedites persistence, eliminating expensive persist barriers.
key_novelty: Whole-system compiler-directed epoch partitioning that extends crash consistency guarantees across the entire software stack with minimal hardware support.
contributions: Compiler/architecture codesign framework for lightweight whole-system persistence
Software-stack-wide partitioning into recoverable epochs for crash consistency
Advanced compiler optimizations for minimal register checkpointing
6% average runtime overhead versus state-of-the-art approaches

metrics.other: 6% average runtime overhead across 37 SPEC/HPC applications
